g.text: 1. Free the caps: clamp the middle of each stock tube with locking pliers and

text.style: font-size: 6.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #ffffff

g.text: squeeze it oval. The glue seal breaks and the caps pop off. The clear tubes

text.style: font-size: 6.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #ffffff

g.text: are sacrificed; caps and inserts survive.

text.style: font-size: 4.8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #b9cfe8
font-size: 6.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #ffffff

g.text: 2. Buy clear acrylic tube Ø14 OD × Ø12 ID. gbrich bought 305 mm, enough for

text.style: font-size: 6.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #ffffff
font-size: 4.8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #b9cfe8
font-size: 6.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #ffffff

g.text: 3. Cut to 23 mm: the insert is 22 mm long without its nub, leaving 1 mm of

text.style: font-size: 6.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #ffffff

g.text: play. A 60T fine-cut mitre saw gave square ends; a junior hacksaw struggled.

text.style: font-size: 4.8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #b9cfe8
font-size: 6.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #ffffff

g.text: 4. Glue a cap to one end, slide the insert in from the other end, then glue

text.style: font-size: 6.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #ffffff

g.text: that end into the lid. The rebuilt tubes no longer twist-lock.
